name: @breeze/i18n
//exports-locales: The editor imports en.json statically as its fallback layer and code-splits the rest, so the catalogues have to be reachable as a subpath. The server does not use this — it reads the same directory from disk, because it needs to enumerate what shipped rather than name one file.
//files: Inert here — every workspace package is private and consumed through pnpm symlinks, so nothing is ever packed. Kept for shape consistency with @breeze/schema only. What actually decides whether locales/ reaches production is the Dockerfile's runtime stage, which copies per directory: @breeze/i18n needs a COPY line for locales as well as one for dist, and missing it fails silently because the English merge layer hides it.
//react: React is a peer, not a dependency: the server and the esbuild client bundles import @breeze/i18n and must not pull React in behind them. Only the editor imports @breeze/i18n/react.
